CITY OF SOUTH PASADENA
  CITY COUNCIL CLOSED SESSION
  SPECIAL MEETING AMENDED AGENDA

  Emergency Operations Center (EOC)
  South Pasadena Fire Department
  817 Mound Avenue, South Pasadena, CA 91030

  Wednesday, February 3, 2021, at 6:29 p.m.

  NOTICE ON PUBLIC PARTICIPATION & ACCESSIBILITY

 Pursuant to Section 3 of Executive Order N-29-20, issued by Governor Newsom on March 17, 2020,
 the special Closed Session meeting of the City Council for February 3, 2021 will be conducted
 remotely and held by video conference.

 Please be advised that pursuant to the Executive Order, and to ensure the health and safety of the
 public by limiting human contact that could spread the COVID-19 virus, the Emergency Operations
 Center will not be open for the meeting. Council Members will be participating remotely and will
 not be physically present.

CALL TO ORDER:  Mayor Diana Mahmud
ROLL CALL:  Councilmembers Jack Donovan, Jon Primuth, and Evelyn
  G. Zneimer; Mayor Pro Tem Michael Cacciotti and Mayor
  Diana Mahmud

 PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD FOR CLOSED SESSION ITEMS ONLY
 The City Council welcomes public input. If you would like to comment on a Closed Session agenda
 item, members of the public may submit their comments for City Council consideration by one of
 the following options:

 Option 1:
  1. Dial (626) 322-2344 and leave a recording of your public comment. Please state your name;
  if you are providing public comment for open or closed session; and, the agenda item
  number. If no agenda item number is provided, your public comment will automatically be
  played under the general public comment portion of the open session meeting. The cutoff
  time for public comment to be submitted via phone recording is 3 p.m. the day of the Council
  Meeting. (The 3 p.m. deadline will allow staff time to appropriately compile the recordings
  and ready them to be played at the Council meeting).
 Option 2:
  2. Email your public comments to ccpubliccomment@southpasadenaca.gov.  Public
  Comments received in writing will not be read aloud at the meeting. Written public

 PRESENTATIONS

3. February 2021 as Black History Month Proclamation

  Mayor Mahmud read the proclamation declaring February 2021 as Black History Month. She
  announced South Pasadena Public Library will co-sponsoring a video chat with Richard
  Rothstein to discuss his book The Color of Law: A Forgotten History of How Our Government
  Segregated America on February 4, 2021, at 6:30 p.m. and noted additional details can be found
  website.

4. Eagle Scout Award Certificate of Achievement for Michael R. Johnston

  Mayor Mahmud presented the Eagle Scout Award Certificate to Michael R. Johnston (in
  attendance via Zoom) and provided remarks. Mr. Johnston thanked City Council and noted his
  project was to update the Aquatic Center at the East Los Angeles Boys and Girls Club and
  provide much-needed safety equipment.

5. Metro Gold Line Presentation  Paul Leon, Mayor for City of Ontario

  Construction Authority. He reported construction is complete through the Azusa-Pacific/Citrus
  Station. He noted the next station to be completed is Glendora and advised construction is fully-
  funded through Pomona. Lastly, he noted the goal is to get the Gold Line to Ontario Airport.

  Mayor Leon reported there were 21 at grade crossings that require major utilities rerouting and
  upgrades. He anticipates construction through Pomona will be completed in 2024. He reported
  an additional $450 million will be required to extend the Gold Line from Pomona to Claremont
  and an additional $15 million will be required to extend to Montclair. He expressed confidence
  the funding will be found to extend through Montclair.

  Councilmember Primuth requested Mayor Leon provide some video of the construction to
  highlight the work being done. Mayor Leon noted he will provide a video compilation to the
  City Council.

  Mayor Mahmud expressed her support for extending the Gold Line to Ontario Airport.

COMMUNICATIONS

7. Councilmembers Communications

  Councilmember Primuth reported attendance at the retirement drive-by for Liliana Torres and
  wished her well. He also reported attendance at the Ad Hoc Finance Committee meeting. He
  thanked Interim City Manager Sean Joyce for including community discussion on CalTrans
  homes on Bonita Drive. He encouraged City Council to move to convene a subcommittee to
  create a Core Value Statement that would be adopted by the City and would be part and parcel
  of how the City Manager is evaluated.

  Mayor Mahmud explained the Brown Act compliance requirements if a subcommittee were to
  be created. Mayor Mahmud suggested two members of the City Council work informally to
  develop such a statement and then have the statement circulated for review by other
  Councilmembers. Councilmember Primuth  .

  Councilmember Donovan stressed the importance of residents wearing face masks and
  encouraged the community to look into obtaining the COVID-19 vaccine. He reported
  attendance at the recent Youth Commission meeting and noted they intend to meet regularly.
  He reported the Chamber of Commerce and the City are still discussing a joint proposal which
  is planned to be presented to City Council on February 16 th.

  Councilmember Zneimer reported attendance at a meeting with the Anti-Racism Committee
  of South Pasadena (ARC) where they expressed concern regarding the Police Chief
  recruitment effort and conduct of certain police officers. She reported ARC requests a
  resolution from South Pasadena acknowledging the City was once a Sundown Town. She
  thanked Wes Reutimann from Active San Gabriel Valley for the presentation he will be making
  this evening. She reported she met with Sierra Madre Mayor Rachelle Arizmendi who is the
  Chair for the Foothill Economic Development Consortium.

   Mayor Mahmud seconded Councilmember Zneimer's request for Council consideration of a
  resolution acknowledging South Pasadena as a former Sundown Town.

  Mayor Pro Tem Cacciotti reported attendance at the Natural Resources and Environmental
  Commission (NREC) meeting. He thanked Interim City Manager Joyce for facilitating a
  meeting with Los Angeles County Supervisor Hilda Solis and Los Angeles City Council
  Member Kevin de León to discuss CalTrans vacant properties. He presented photos of various
  community activities.

  Mayor Mahmud requested a second for the City to send a letter of support asking the County
  to adopt recommendations contained in a white paper on the administration of homeless funds
  prepared by the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG) which recommends
  more flexibility in the allocation of funding. Mayor Pro Tem Cacciotti seconded Mayor

  Mayor Mahmud reported attendance at a Special Meeting of the Planning Commission
  regarding consideration of an Inclusionary Ordinance. She reported Los Angeles County has
  approved the reopening of outdoor dining. She encouraged residents to wear a mask while
  participating in outdoor dining. She encouraged residents to visit vaccinatelacounty.com to
  register for a vaccine and/or receive email updates.

15. Authorize the Interim City Manager to Request Authorization from Metro to Repurpose

  Recovery

  Mayor Mahmud announced written comment was received by the Chamber of Commerce on
  this item. She noted there were two additional documents for the item and requested any motion
  made for approval reference the revised documents. City Council concurred.

  Planning and Community Development Director Joanna Hankamer introduced Wes Reutimann
  from Active San Gabriel Valley. Mr. Reutimann provided a brief overview of the Metro Open
  Streets Program and noted the inaugural event took place on March 5, 2017.

  Mr. Reutimann reported the Metro Board of Directors authorized Open Streets grantees to
  repurpose existing grant awards to support COVID-19 Response/Recovery measures in the
  public right of way in June 2020 and provided a brief overview of eligible project types. He
  provided an overview of the submission process and reported the deadline to spend funds was
  June 30, 2021, but has been extended to December 31, 2021. He provided a brief overview of
  local examples of repurposing from adjacent municipalities.

  Mr. Reutimann reported the current proposal for South Pasadena would be to utilize funds to
  create and support safer outdoor business and vending opportunities and slow streets. He
  provided samples of signage from other cities. Lastly, he reported Metro should hold another
  Request for Event Proposals for Cycle 4 and held possibly in Fall 2021 which would make the
  event time from 2022 to 2023.
